result.keywords: Emerging intelligent systems increasingly combine nonvolatile resistive devices with light-responsive soft materials to enable adaptive computation and actuation in compact platforms. Resistive memory arrays can support vector-matrix operations for low-power neural acceleration, while photo-responsive polymer structures provide coordinated mechanical motion under optical control. This article surveys device concepts, circuit integration, and system-level organization for hybrid in-memory computing and soft robotic elements. Emphasis is placed on synaptic behavior, feedback-enabled actuation, and scalable architectures suitable for biomimetic sensing, learning, and movement in distributed edge systems.
result.title: Adaptive Resistive Photo-Synaptic Systems for Soft In-Memory Robotics.
